title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting (December quotas) — the last decision inside the reported Q4 pause
source: EST: cadence projection off the seven participating countries' own primary. opec.org/pr-detail/1835613-6-september-2026.html, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200), records that Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman 'decided to maintain September 2026 required production for October 2026', states they 'will continue to hold monthly meetings to review market conditions', and closes with the verbatim sentence 'The next meeting will be held on 4 October 2026.' The observed cadence is the FIRST SUNDAY of each month, 5 for 5 on the record with each date named verbatim in the prior release — 2026-06-07, 2026-07-05, 2026-08-02, 2026-09-06, 2026-10-04 — and the first Sunday of November 2026 is 2026-11-01. NO SOURCE NAMES A NOVEMBER DATE. The 09-06 release names only 10-04; opec.org's own meetings and press-release indexes both returned 403 to curl and 402 to WebFetch on 2026-09-09, and a targeted search for a published November date returned nothing 2026-dated. Filed estimate on three counts, none of which is doubt about the cadence: market-events-data.ts defines no trusted source prefix for opec.org, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the date itself is PROJECTED rather than published. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), promoting the single sibling proposal proposals/opec-plus-meeting-2026-11-01.from-jobs-2026-11-06.json (that print's D-58 adjacency sweep) with its title amended: 'December quotas' is retained and the structural role added. What makes this instance different from opec-plus-meeting-2026-10-04 is that it is the LAST of the three decisions inside the reported whole-Q4 pause (10-04 set November, this sets December), so it is the edge of the window rather than its middle — the point at which a pause either ends or gets extended into the 2027 baseline regime, and the successor meeting (first Sunday of December, 2026-12-06, deliberately NOT proposed: projecting off a projection is not sourcing) would set January 2027, the first month governed by the new baselines. Second structural fact, and the reason this entry is worth a ledger of its own: Iran's 2027 MSC baseline is reported to be set from the average of its August, September and October 2026 production, so that measurement window CLOSES 2026-10-31 — the day before this meeting — with the number fixed at war-suppressed levels (US export blockade since mid-April; Kharg Island, which handles up to 90% of Iran's exports, the site of US tanker strikes on 09-05 and 09-08). 11-01 is the first OPEC+ forum at which that number can no longer move. The averaging rule is SECONDARY-sourced (Argus/IndexBox/Reuters-derived) and labelled as such wherever it is used. Impact `medium` mirrors opec-plus-meeting-2026-09-06 and opec-plus-meeting-2026-10-04 and reflects the base case (a third consecutive non-decision), not the consequence if the pause breaks at its edge. Corridor: 11-01 carries 39 tracked ids inside +/-5 days — FOMC 10-28, GDP-Q3-advance and PCE 10-29, ECI 10-30, ISM-mfg 11-02, midterm-elections-2026-11-03, ISM-services and the Treasury refunding 11-04, jobs 11-06 — which makes this the least consequential dated item in its own corridor and its Monday cash read (11-02) confounded within one session.
